title: OA ChatCompletions gateway hydrator: request shaping + response normalization for streaming & tool-calls
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: Customers using the OpenAI Chat Completions API expect parity when migrating to Redwood’s /chat endpoint. Differences in streaming framing, function/tool call signaling, and structured output conventions cause breakage for adapters and SDKs downstream.

Goal: Implement a lightweight gateway component (hydrator) that accepts OpenAI ChatCompletions-style requests and produces Redwood-internal request shapes optimized for streaming, KV cache reuse, and tool/function calling while preserving semantics so responses can be mapped back to OpenAI-compatible streaming fragments and final response payloads.

Scope: Request shaping (role/name/message arrays -> internal prompt + metadata), streaming event mapping (delta tokens, function_call start/update/end), structured output enforcement (JSON block detection and validation), and backwards-compatible response normalization for non-streaming clients. Do not change existing public Redwood API surface; implement as an internal compatibility layer behind a feature flag.
Out of scope: Full OpenAI API surface (edits/images), advanced safety normalization, and schema-validated model outputs beyond basic JSON detection/repair.
acceptance_criteria: 1) The gateway accepts OpenAI ChatCompletions requests and returns the same HTTP status semantics for invalid inputs as the OpenAI baseline (400/401/429/500 equivalents).

2) Streaming responses from Redwood models can be reassembled into OpenAI-style SSE/HTTP2 fragments that include 'role' and partial 'content' deltas and emit function_call events when models produce tool invocation markers.

3) Function/tool calling: gateway extracts function definitions and ensures the internal call payload includes schema + name mapping; the returned function payload is serialized into the OpenAI-compatible function_call structure on finalization.

4) Structured output: if client requests a JSON schema via function definitions or system instructions, common malformed JSON outputs (unclosed braces, trailing commas) are repaired heuristically in the gateway with configurable aggressiveness, and repairs are annotated in response metadata.
5) E2E tests show <5% added tail-latency at 95th percentile for typical chat workloads when gateway is enabled; flagged performance regressions must have mitigation plan before rollout.
6) Feature flag gate (oa-compat-gateway) allows staged rollout per-customer and per-region.
technical_notes: Architecture: stateless HTTP gateway service (or lightweight middleware inside routing plane) that maps OA request -> Redwood request. Must be horizontally scalable and instrumented for token-level telemetry and request shape histograms.

Streaming model: map internal streaming tokens to OpenAI 'delta' fragments. For function_call streams emit a 'function_call' object with 'name' and incremental 'arguments' fragments following OpenAI framing conventions.
KV caching: preserve message ids and prefix tokens to enable cache hits across OA-shaped requests. Add a normalized message_digest header for cache lookup.

JSON repair: use a small sanitizer that attempts to close unbalanced braces/brackets, remove trailing commas, and try single-pass JSON5 -> JSON conversion. Annotate repairs in 'x-oa-compat-warning' header and in response.metadata.repair_hint.
Security: sanitize function definitions to prevent injection of unsafe URLs or shell-like commands. Mark security_review_required=true for the gateway initial rollout.

Backward compatibility: maintain original query params and headers where possible (accepts openai-client idempotency keys and propagates them). Map Redwood error codes to OpenAI-like codes for compatibility.
design_decisions: 1) Implement as routing middleware rather than a separate microservice to reduce RPC hops; exception: if CPU work from JSON repair impacts host, flip to separate service.
2) Use delta-first mapping for streaming to minimize buffering. Avoid reassembling full output in gateway except for function_call finalization steps.
3) Keep repair heuristics configurable: off for strict customers, conservative by default, aggressive only for self-serve customers who opt in.
4) Expose per-request diagnostic headers to help SDKs map fragments to original OA indices.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag rollout to internal QA with synthetic OA traffic (cycle 2026-W09).
2) Canary in region us-west-2 for low-volume customers; monitor latency/cost and functionality for 72h.
3) Invite a small set of customers via support to trial the compatibility gateway with opt-in toggle.
4) Gradual ramp to GA over 4 weeks if no regressions >2x error rate or >10% latency degradation on P50/P95.
5) Post-mortem and learnings consolidated in Confluence after GA.
qa_steps: Unit tests for request -> internal mapping for role/name variants.
Integration tests: streaming token replay tests that assert OpenAI SSE fragment equivalence.
Property tests for function_call incremental framing and finalization.
Chaos tests: simulate partial HTTP client disconnects to ensure gateway state cleanup and model invocation abort semantics.
Performance benchmarks comparing baseline path vs gateway path across 10k synthetic requests.
